title: Why the compressed swap timing run stopped
headline: The shared compression library passed its functional checks. The timing tool rejected the first read after it saw two successful decompressions in the same observation window.

sections.title: Why time compressed swap
sections.lead: A memory page can be stored as a smaller compressed copy. Restoring it takes work, so the experiment measures how long the application waits.

blocks.text: The shared library moves compression and storage code behind one interface. The experiment tests whether existing behavior survives the change.

sections.title: Where compressed swap operates
sections.lead: An application reads a page that is no longer resident in working memory.

sections.title: What the timing observer sees
sections.lead: A return probe reports successful decompression for the benchmark process.

sections.title: Shared compression and diagnostic capture
sections.lead: The candidate uses the shared library. The follow-up also records the original bytes when a timing observation is rejected.

sections.title: Isolate the timing tool
sections.lead: Keep the tool's non-target memory resident and prove that the target region is still eligible for swap. Use the same observer on both kernels before collecting any new comparison.

blocks.text: Independent XSwap still needs its guest driver and physical-route evidence. Pressure-driven migration depends on an independently verified XSwap frontend.

patches.takeaway: Free compressed objects through the shared library

subtitle: A functional rerun and a trace of the first failed timing observation.

verdict_tiles.label: Function
verdict_tiles.note: Data, concurrency and cleanup passed again.

verdict_tiles.label: Timing
verdict_tiles.note: Two decompressions appeared for the first timed access.

verdict_tiles.label: Decision
verdict_tiles.note: Verify its own pages stay resident during testing.

results_lead: The original kernel reproduced the timing failure in a valid virtual machine. Its first observation contained two successful return records for the same process and no missed probe.
results_detail: The trace reader completed without truncation. The observer requires exactly one decode per timed page, so the workload stopped before collecting usable measurements. The trace does not identify the page address for either return.

chart.takeaway: The observation contained an extra decoder return
